finding.message: Domain class Subscription holds infrastructure SystemClock via FLOWS_TO (clock)

answer.explanation: The Subscription domain class imports the SystemClock outbound adapter (src/domain/subscription.ts:1). It also creates its own instance in a private field (line 4) and calls clock.now() inside isActive() (line 9) to compare the current time with endsAt. So the domain core is tied to a concrete infrastructure adapter. Its active/inactive logic can't be driven by a substitute time source, and the dependency runs from the core out to the adapter layer instead of inward. FF-P06 flags this because a domain class holds an infrastructure type through a FLOWS_TO edge (the clock field). Accepted ADR-0009 says the core must not import SystemClock and should depend on a Clock port in src/domain that the adapter implements. ADR-0002 allowed the direct import, but ADR-0009 has superseded it, so that permission no longer applies. The fix is small and clear: define a Clock port in src/domain, have SystemClock implement it, and inject the port into Subscription instead of creating the adapter inside it.

Subscription is a domain entity in src/domain. It imports the outbound adapter SystemClock (line 1) and creates it in a private field (line 4). It then calls clock.now() inside isActive() (line 9) to decide whether the subscription has ended. So the domain core holds a concrete infrastructure object through a FLOWS_TO (clock) edge and calls SystemClock.now through a CALLS edge. That is a dependency pointing from the core out to an adapter, which is what FF-P06 forbids. It also hard-wires real time into the entity, so isActive() can't be tested with a fixed time without patching the adapter. ADR-0002 once allowed this direct import, but it is marked superseded. ADR-0009 is Accepted and says the core must not import SystemClock or any other adapter. Instead it should depend on a Clock port in src/domain, which the outbound adapter implements. The code still follows the superseded decision and was never moved to the port.

finding.message: src/domain/subscription.ts (domain) imports against the allowed direction from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts (adapters-outbound)

answer.explanation: src/domain/subscription.ts imports SystemClock from the outbound adapter layer (line 1). It creates an instance in a field (line 4) and calls clock.now() inside isActive() (line 9). This makes the domain core depend on a concrete infrastructure adapter, which reverses the allowed direction: adapters may depend on the domain, but the domain must not depend on adapters. FF-S01 flags it for that reason. ADR-0002 once allowed this exact import, but it is marked "Superseded by ADR-0009". ADR-0009 is Accepted and says the domain core must not import SystemClock or any other adapter. It must instead depend on a Clock port in src/domain that the outbound adapter implements. The code still follows the old, superseded decision. The fix is small and well defined: add a Clock interface in src/domain, have SystemClock implement it, and inject it into Subscription instead of creating SystemClock inside the class.

finding.message: Core file src/domain/subscription.ts imports from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts in adapters-outbound

answer.explanation: The domain entity Subscription in src/domain/subscription.ts imports SystemClock from the outbound adapter layer on line 1. On line 4 it creates the clock itself (new SystemClock()), and isActive() on line 9 calls SystemClock.now(). The graph slice shows the same coupling: a CALLS edge to SystemClock.now and a FLOWS_TO edge to SystemClock. FF-S04 flags this because the dependency points the wrong way. A core file depends on a concrete adapter instead of an abstraction that the core owns. The domain is therefore tied to the real system time, cannot be tested with a controlled clock, and cannot be built or reasoned about without the adapter layer. ADR-0002 once allowed this import, but its status is "Superseded by ADR-0009". The accepted ADR-0009 forbids the core from importing SystemClock or any other adapter and requires a Clock port in src/domain, which the outbound adapter implements. This code has not been migrated to that decision.
